title: Staying Safe: Roads, Fire and Online
summary: Simple rules that can protect you at home, on the road and on the internet.

steps.title: On the road
sentences: Always walk on the footpath, and cross at a zebra crossing or where there is a signal.
Look right, look left and look right again before you cross.
When you ride in a car or on a two-wheeler, wear a seat belt or a helmet every time.

steps.title: Fire safety
sentences: Never play with matches, lighters or crackers.
If there is a fire, get out, stay out and call 101 for the fire brigade, or 112, India's emergency number.
If clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll.

steps.title: Online safety
sentences: Do not share your address, school or phone number with people you only know online.
Never share your passwords, except with your parents.
If something online makes you feel scared or uncomfortable, tell a trusted adult at once.

steps.title: Trust your feelings
sentences: If something feels wrong, you can say no and walk away.
Know the phone number of a trusted adult by heart.
In India, Childline 1098 is a free helpline for any child who needs help.

facts: 112 is the all-in-one emergency number across India.
A helmet can greatly reduce the risk of serious head injury.
Strong passwords are long and mix words, numbers and symbols.

quiz.q: Which number is for the fire brigade in India?
What should you do if you feel unsafe online?
quiz.why: Tell a trusted adult right away.

quiz.q: What is the all-in-one emergency number in India?

notes: Helpline numbers are as given by the Government of India at the time of writing; check that they are still in use.
